children: Abu Dhabi leads most major Gulf markets higher, with its benchmark index gaining 1.3%. The Dubai Financial Market General Index rises 0.6%, while Qatar's QE Index bucks the trend, falling 0.5%. Investors are watching for signs of U.S.-Iran diplomatic progress around the U.N. General Assembly. Qatar faces increased funding needs after disruption to LNG exports sharply reduced government revenue, MUFG says. The country raised $3 billion in international bonds this week, with orders exceeding $7.7 billion and the deal pricing around 30 basis points tighter than initial guidance. Prolonged LNG disruption could keep Qatar's borrowing needs elevated, MUFG says. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
